item.title: Purim Katan
item.description:
Tonight and tomorrow is the 14th of Adar Rishon, Purim Katan, which comes about once in three years and is not the same as the local Purim Sheni some towns keep for their own miracles. The Gemara puts the main Purim in the second Adar, next to Pesah, and the Mishnah says only the Megillah and gifts to the poor are missing in the first. There is no fasting or eulogy, and the Rema, closing Orah Hayim, recommends a festive meal: it is always good to be merry.

item.title: 2: Daily Halacha: The Origins and Meaning of Purim Katan, Minor Purim
item.description:
Why does a Jewish leap year add a second Adar, seven times in nineteen years? It keeps the lunar calendar in step with the sun so that Pesah falls in spring, and the Gemara puts Purim in the second Adar to place one redemption next to the other. The name Purim Katan is only a few hundred years old, borrowed from the Mishnah's Pesah Katan, and is not the same as the local Purim Sheni of towns that were saved.

item.title: Further points on Purim Katan & In Which Adar to commemorate a Nahala
item.description:
Purim Katan is kept on both the 14th and the 15th of Adar Rishon, with no Tahanun, fasting or eulogies, and the Rema mentions a festive meal, which the Kaf HaHayim extends to the 15th as well. Then the nahala of one who died in an ordinary Adar: the Shulhan Arukh and the Sefaradim keep it in the second Adar, the Rema and most Ashkenazim in the first, and a family with both customs may keep both.

item.title: 4: Daily Halacha: When to Commemorate a Nahalah in a Leap Year
item.description:
When is the nahala of someone who died in Adar of an ordinary year kept in a leap year? The Shulhan Arukh says the second Adar, the main month, since we do not bring sad things forward, and this is the Sefaradi custom; the Rema says the first, since a misvah should be done at the first chance. One who belongs to both communities may keep both, and Purim Katan itself has no fasting, eulogies or Tahanun.

item.title: 5: Daily Halacha: A Thought for Purim Katan: Finding Excuses to Be Cheerful
item.description:
Is there a misvah of a festive meal on Purim Katan? The Mishnah says only the Megillah and gifts to the poor separate the two months of Adar, and some Rishonim in France, quoted by Tosafot, held a seudah in the first Adar, but the Rambam and the Shulhan Arukh rule there is none. The Rema closes Orah Hayim with tov lev mishteh tamid: even without an obligation, a good heart looks for every chance to be happy and thank Hashem.
